name: mqdd_starv_20
oracle_ref: mq-deadline write starvation: ascending read sweep until the starved>=2 flip, then ALL writes as one contiguous ascending epoch, then the read sweep resumes ascending (no reset)
notes: STARVED-COUNTER WALK (q_mq_deadline.bpf.c local_dispatch_prio; fifo_batch=16; IOSCHED_MQD_MAX_READ_STARVATION=2; entry dir=READ/batching=0/starved=0 from init_hctx): a direction selection runs when batching reaches 16 or the current-dir lane is empty. A selection with BOTH lanes non-empty evaluates `starved++ >= 2` (post-increment): evaluations 1 and 2 compare 0<2 and 1<2 -> dir=READ and the 16-read sweep epochs continue; evaluation 3 reads starved=2 -> 2>=2 TRUE -> dir=WRITE = THE WRITE-STARVATION FLIP, never exercised by any registered case before. Post-flip every mixed selection re-chooses WRITE (starved only grows), so all queued writes dispatch as contiguous ascending C-LOOK epochs of 16; when the write lane empties, the selection takes dir=READ WITHOUT touching starved (write_count==0 short-circuits both starved++ and the reset), and the read sweep resumes ascending. REACHABILITY (this is the third and final derivation iteration; the first two are preserved as evidence): the flip needs 3 CONSECUTIVE mixed selections = 16*3+1 dispatches with reads+writes resident and no read-empty->write selection in between. (1) It needs a deep queue: 4KB arrivals match the device completion rate under QEMU's 200MB burst bucket (unthrottled ~2GB/s), so requests are 128KB (completion ~64us >> submission ~3-5us/SQE measured) to saturate the ~256 virtio driver tags mid-submission and stack a mixed backlog of hundreds. (2) It needs the state machine to actually RUN: with ascending arrivals every C-LOOK tree dispatch victim IS the FIFO front; the dispatched node stays in the FIFO as stale, the next continuation call is consumed by the stale scavenge (lane_collect_stale_front -> gc_has_work -> return 0), and the kernel then dispatches via the policy evacuate hook fallback (scx_io_dispatch_request: `if (!rq_ptr && ops->evacuate)`), which bypasses dir/batching/starved entirely — measured sel_mixed=0 with a 420-deep mixed queue (results/mqdd_phase3/selstats). DESCENDING arrival order makes the sweep victim != FIFO front, so the continuation runs clean, batching advances, selections fire every 16 dispatches. (3) The writes must arrive AFTER the sweep starts (submitted last) so the selections are mixed: starved bumps from 0 on the first mixed selection after write arrival and flips on the 3rd (<=48 sweep dispatches after the writes queue up). The sel_stats_map telemetry (q_mqdd_sel_stats, added in Phase-3 to the policy) shows sel_flip>0 for this trace. ASSERTED (partial): (a) all 800 sectors issue (512-sector same-op gaps, disjoint read/write ranges => merge-immune); (b) write lane strictly ascending — the writes all issue in ONE contiguous epoch (their arrivals are descending, so the write continuation is also scavenge-free); (c) DISCRIMINATOR: ALL 96 writes issue BEFORE the read sectors at ascending-sweep positions 180..230 — the flip fires at sweep dispatch <=~64 (48 + write-arrival skew), so positions 180..230 (2.8x margin) issue after the write epoch ONLY IF the flip interrupted the sweep; a NO-FLIP run (all reads then writes — e.g. the evacuate-driven behavior of an ascending-arrival trace, or the M03/M04 lane pattern) dispatches those reads before every write and fails this constraint. Read-lane monotonicity is intentionally NOT asserted: the pre-saturation prefix (~256-330 arrivals while tags are free) issues in DESCENDING arrival order; the sweep itself is ascending (and the post-flip suffix ascending) but the compare engine cannot express range-restricted monotonicity. expected_dispatch_order is a representative sequence (320-descending prefix, sweep to flip at 64, contiguous write epoch, ascending suffix); its VALUES are illustrative — the partial constraints are authoritative; its length (800) tells compare_expect.py to consider all 800 window issues.
